title: S&P DJI December quarterly rebalance takes effect at the open — S&P 500/100/400/600 membership and float changes, implemented at the 2026-12-18 close
source: EST: forward derivation of the owner's own effective-date wording, re-fetched this session from FOUR December instances rather than inherited. All four fetched direct from S&P Dow Jones Indices' own newsroom 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200), each verbatim 'effective prior to the open of trading on ...': the 2022-12-02 release (55,025 bytes) — 'Monday, December 19' against a third Friday of 2022-12-16; the 2023-12-01 release (70,156 bytes) — 'Monday, December 18', third Friday 2023-12-15, its table rows stamped 'Dec. 18, 2023'; the 2024-12-06 release (63,098 bytes) — 'Monday, December 23', third Friday 2024-12-20, rows stamped 'December 23, 2024'; the 2025-12-05 release (79,722 bytes) — 'Monday, December 22', third Friday 2025-12-19, rows stamped 'Dec 22, 2025'. One sentence, four consecutive Decembers, one geometry: the effective open is the Monday after that quarter's third Friday. December 2026's Fridays are the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th, so the third Friday is 2026-12-18 — independently tracked as opex-2026-12-18 on the OCC calendar — and the effective open is Monday 2026-12-21. No US market holiday falls between them (Christmas Day 2026-12-25 is itself a Friday, after both dates), so the holiday-shift exception that moved June 2022 to a Tuesday does not bite here. Filed estimate on the same three counts the sibling entries record, none of them date doubt: the December 2026 release does not exist yet (S&P DJI announces after the close of the first Friday two weeks prior, i.e. 2026-12-04, tracked as sp-rebalance-proforma-2026-12-04), the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for an index owner's own published schedule, and this lane may not self-confirm. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), which read the single proposal carrying this id (proposals/sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-12-21.from-sp-rebalance-reference-close-2026-12-11.json) in full first, then re-fetched and re-derived every claim rather than inheriting it. Ledger: docs/research/events/sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-12-21.md. THIS ENTRY EXISTS OVER TWO EXPLICIT DECLINES AND THE RESEARCH ADJUDICATES THEM. Both sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21 and sp-rebalance-proforma-2026-12-04 recorded a deliberate refusal to file the December effective open, on an index-level SPY null; the sp-rebalance-reference-close-2026-12-11 sweep filed it anyway. The decliners were RIGHT ABOUT THE DATE and the filing still paid for itself, because the research it forced measured the one cell of this chain nobody had opened. WHAT THIS SESSION MEASURED THAT NO SIBLING DID — the CONSTITUENT-level behaviour of the two flow sessions. Rebuilding the owner's release archive independently (899 dated releases 2022-05-06 to 2026-09-04, 17 of 18 quarterly cycles announcing, June 2025 a no-op, 700 constituent rows — every count an exact match to the proforma sibling reached by a different data route) and pricing it against each tier's own ETF from Yahoo query1 bars (460 of 513 symbols; the 53 failures are delisted names), three sessions of one panel under one method: the ANNOUNCEMENT reaction is n=582, +2.31% mean directional excess, 410/582 correctly signed, exact sign p<0.001%, 1.84x relative turnover; the IMPLEMENTATION FRIDAY is n=504, -0.03%, 256/504, p=75.5% — and 10.61x relative turnover; the EFFECTIVE OPEN, this event's own session, is n=548, +0.09%, 280/548, p=63.8%, 1.77x. EVERY TIER FAILS ITS SIGN TEST ON THE EFFECTIVE OPEN (600 additions 79/162 p=81.4%, 600 deletions 77/147 p=62.1%, 500 additions 14/35 p=31.1%, 500 deletions 16/33 p=100.0%), and December alone is no different (47/98, p=76.2%). So this date is a null at BOTH units of observation — index level (SPY effective-open return 41/84 negative, p~91%, independently replicated this session) and constituent level — which is a strictly stronger refusal than either decliner could make, and the last place a signature could have hidden. THE ONE DURABLE OUTPUT IS AN EXECUTION NUMBER, and it is constituent-level rather than index-level: an index-change name trades a MEDIAN 16.2x-17.5x its own trailing-60 median volume on the implementation Friday, against its tier ETF's 1.45x and against a placebo second-Friday-of-the-same-month at 1.26x-1.50x — the largest single-session flow event in these names' year, on a return distribution indistinguishable from a coin flip. That sharpens rather than confirms the September sibling's 'turnover is the discriminator' reading: turnover discriminates flow from no-flow, not winners from losers. Symbols deliberately EMPTY: the December roster does not exist until the 2026-12-04 release, and the effect this research found is announcement-dated, not effective-dated. ONE ADJACENT PROPOSED, one declined on the record: PROPOSED ndx-annual-reconstitution-announcement-2026-12-11, methodology-dated from Nasdaq's own PDF and entirely untracked for 2026 (only the 2027 instance is proposed) — it also covers the NDX QUARTERLY rebalance, whose effective date the 2027 sibling did not name and which lands on this same open. DECLINED ndx-annual-reconstitution-effective-2026-12-21, on the 2027 sibling's own measured QQQ null: filing it would put a second null on a session already tracked. Kind 'sector' matches sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2026-09-21 and -2027-12-20; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
